clock.purpose: The hero device. Reads scroll position back as time, 23:00 to 06:00. Always tabular.

ledger.purpose: The audit's figures. Mono and tabular because they are money being counted, not a technical costume.

say.purpose: The scroll-stopping sentences. Bricolage 700 only; the family carries no other weight on this page.

stamp.purpose: Hour markers and labels. Wide positive tracking, the opposite direction to the display face.

hanzi.purpose: The widget demo. Subset to the ten characters used.

shadows.name: device
shadows.purpose: The phone illustration — the only object on the page that floats.

shadows.name: widget
shadows.purpose: The widget sitting on the phone's screen.

motion.name: scroll
motion.value: Lenis lerp 0.095, wheelMultiplier 0.95, synced to the GSAP ticker via lenis.raf(t*1000) and lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)
motion.purpose: The scroll feel itself. Skipped entirely on coarse pointers so phones keep native scrolling.

motion.name: hours
motion.value: linear RGB interpolation between consecutive chapter stops, sampled at scrollY + innerHeight*0.5
motion.purpose: The continuous ground. Read point is mid-viewport so the colour matches what is actually being read.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: SplitText lines with mask, yPercent 115 to 0, expo.out 1.05s, stagger 0.075, once
motion.purpose: Masked line reveals. The genre's signature gesture.

motion.name: audit
motion.value: pinned 2400px, scrub 0.6, rows staggered 0.9s apart with figures counting on power2.out
motion.purpose: The one scrubbed sequence. It cannot advance without the visitor, which is the point.

motion.name: headswap
motion.value: discrete class toggle when dawn's top passes 72px, colour transition 0.25s
motion.purpose: A switch, never a fade — fading the header through the inversion would cross the unreadable midpoint.

components.name: Chapter
components.description: One hour-stop on the path. Declares its colours as data attributes for the engine and as CSS variables for itself, so the page is a correct readable sequence with JavaScript disabled.
components.html: 02:30 — the audit
components.css: .ds-ch { position: relative; background: var(--ch-bg); color: var(--ch-fg); --fg: var(--ch-fg); --dim: var(--ch-dim); --accent: var(--ch-accent); padding: 9rem 0; } html.smooth .ds-ch { background: transparent; } .ds-stamp { margin: 0 0 2rem; font: 400 .75rem/1 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; letter-spacing: .16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Ledger
components.description: The audit. Rows start dim and post as the scrub advances; charged and settled cancel; the balance lands on zero above an accent rule.
components.css: .ds-ledger { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 6rem auto; gap: .5rem 1rem; padding: .75rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--dim) 28%, transparent); font-size: .9375rem; } .ds-row span:last-child { text-align: right; } .ds-bal { border-bottom: 0; border-top: 2px solid var(--accent); margin-top: .5rem; padding-top: 1rem; font-size: 1.5rem; color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Masked Line
components.description: SplitText line masking. Each line rides up out of its clip; text stays selectable and screen-reader intact, and is fully visible if the script never runs.
components.css: .ln__mask { overflow: hidden; display: block; } /* JS: SplitText.create(el, { type: 'lines', mask: 'lines' }) then gsap.from(split.lines, { yPercent: 115, ease: 'expo.out' }) */

components.name: Send Button
components.description: The single action, in daylight at the foot of the page.
components.css: .ds-send { justify-self: start; background: #1C1611; color: #EFE3D2; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; padding: .8rem 2rem; font: 600 .9375rem/1 'Familjen Grotesk', sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background .25s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), color .25s; } .ds-send:hover { background: #9A4415; color: #FFF7EE; }

components.name: Ruled Field
components.description: Form fields are ruled lines, never boxes — the page is a ledger.
components.css: .ds-fld { display: grid; gap: .5rem; } .ds-fld label { font: 400 .6875rem/1 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--dim); } .ds-fld input { font: 400 1rem/1.5 'Familjen Grotesk', sans-serif; color: var(--fg); background: transparent; border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--dim) 55%, transparent); border-radius: 0; padding: .4rem 0; width: 100%; } .ds-fld input:focus { outline: 0; border-bottom-color: var(--accent); }

narrative.overview: The page is one night shift. Scroll position maps to time — 23:00 at the top, 06:00 at the bottom — and every visual decision descends from that mapping. The career transition the site exists to communicate is never argued in copy; it is the sunrise. This means the page has no section backgrounds: each chapter declares the colour of its hour and the ground is interpolated continuously between them, so it gets lighter the way a night does rather than cutting between panels. A clock in the header reads the scroll position back, which makes the mapping legible instead of merely atmospheric. There is exactly one pinned moment, the audit, and it is scrubbed rather than played — the visitor's scroll posts each ledger line and settles the balance.
keyCharacteristics: Scroll is time; the palette is a path between six hour-stops, not a set
No section backgrounds — one continuous ground that the whole page shares
The one pinned sequence is scrubbed, so it cannot advance without the visitor
Mono is used for money and time, which is measurement rather than costume
Nothing gates reading: no loader, and native scroll on touch

rules.name: Dawn Arrives, It Never Crossfades
rules.body: Interpolating ground dark-to-light while interpolating text light-to-dark makes them cross and meet; measured contrast at that crossing was 1.31:1. The 06:00 chapter owns an opaque ground and arrives over the night. Any future inversion must do the same, and the header switches by class rather than fading for the same reason.

rules.name: Check Between The Stops
rules.body: The readable values are the interpolated ones, so contrast is sampled across the whole scroll rather than at the chapter stops. Worst case currently 4.88:1 secondary, 11.86:1 primary, across 44 samples.

rules.name: Scrub What Tells A Story
rules.body: A sequence that plays on entry is decoration. The audit is scrubbed so the visitor posts each line and settles the balance themselves; that participation is the whole reason the moment lands.

rules.name: Two Chapters Fill The Viewport
rules.body: The 23:00 opening and the 06:00 dawn are both min-height 100svh. A dawn shorter than the viewport ends the page on a split screen and halves the payoff.

rules.name: Never Pin Taller Than The Viewport
rules.body: The ledger exceeds a phone's height, so pinning it there runs rows under the fixed header. The pin is gated to 48em and up; narrow screens play the same scrubbed sequence unpinned.

rules.name: Two Directions Of Tracking
rules.body: Mono labels run wide (0.14 to 0.3em); the display face runs tight (to -0.06em). The opposing directions keep the two voices distinct at a glance.

dos: Do add a chapter by adding an hour-stop, and check contrast between stops
Do keep mono for measured things only, always tabular
Do let the opening and the dawn fill the viewport
Do keep every reveal's content visible if the script never runs
Do skip smooth scroll on coarse pointers
donts: Don't interpolate ground and text through an inversion
Don't give a chapter its own background panel
Don't pin anything taller than the viewport, and never on a phone
Don't add a loader or anything that gates reading
Don't state what the product record does not confirm
